title: From Awareness to Compliance: Government Social Media Communication and Citizens' Behaviour toward NIN-SIM Registration in Nigeria (Asuquo, Santas & Kente, Feedback International Journal of Communication, 2025)
screen_reason: Cross-sectional survey of 371 Nigerian residents. Although the study's aim is policy compliance, a descriptive share of respondents reporting exposure to misinformation/fake news on social media is reported in the results and in Table 4 (69%), which meets the RECALL criterion (share of survey respondents who say they encountered misleading/false information). No other construct is measured.

estimates.platform: social media (Facebook, WhatsApp, Instagram, X) used for NIN-SIM policy information
estimates.measure_type: % of surveyed residents who reported that misleading/false information on social media was a challenge they encountered around the NIN-SIM policy (labelled 'Exposure to misinformation and fake news' in Table 4)
estimates.value_raw: 69 (Table 4: 'Exposure to misinformation and fake news ... 69'); text: 'About 69% of respondents'
estimates.denominator: 371 residents of Lafia Metropolis, Nigeria, who returned valid questionnaires (availability sample of active social media users exposed to the NIN-SIM campaign)
estimates.definition: Respondent indicated that misleading or false information circulating on social media created confusion about the objectives, procedures and implications of the NIN-SIM registration policy (five-point Likert agreement item, reported as a single percentage)
estimates.misinfo_def: "misleading or false information circulating on social media platforms" / "misinformation and fake news"
estimates.source_quote: About 69% of respondents indicated that misleading or false information circulating on social media platforms created confusion regarding the objectives, procedures, and implications of the NIN-SIM registration policy.
estimates.page_loc: Results and Discussion, section 3.3, p. 285-286; Table 4
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Respondent self-report on a five-point Likert scale; no external verification of what respondents encountered; instrument validity by expert review, reliability by two-week test-retest (no coefficient given)
estimates.moderator_quote: Participants were selected through availability sampling due to the heterogeneity of the urban population and practical constraints associated with large-scale field surveys. ... Out of the 384 questionnaires administered, 371 were successfully retrieved and found valid for analysis.
estimates.notes: Borderline because the item is worded as a barrier/agreement item ('misinformation created confusion') rather than a plain frequency-of-encounter question; the paper's own table labels it 'Exposure to misinformation and fake news', which is why it is coded RECALL/exposure. Topic coded 'other' (a government digital-identity/SIM registration policy - not elections, general news or health). Platform coded multi_platform because the questionnaire concerned social media generally (Facebook, WhatsApp, Instagram, X). Year is the publication year; no data-collection date is reported anywhere in the paper.

missed_or_uncertain: Table 4 also reports 'Difficulty verifying official information online 61' - a verification-capacity item, not an exposure-to-misinformation share, so not extracted. The high-exposure figures (91% exposed to NIN-SIM information, 89% frequent exposure to NCC messages) refer to exposure to OFFICIAL government messages, not misinformation. The 91% compliance-influence figure is an effect measure. No question wording, item stems or response distributions are given for the Table 4 items, so the exact numerator definition for the 69% cannot be verified beyond the sentence quoted.

rob.design: Quantitative cross-sectional survey; availability (convenience) sampling of residents of Lafia Metropolis (est. population 509,300); target of 384 per Krejcie & Morgan table, 371 valid questionnaires retrieved from 384 administered (96.6%); face-to-face administration; five-point Likert items; validity by expert review and reliability by a two-week test-retest with no coefficient reported; descriptive statistics only (frequencies, percentages, means, SDs); no item wording or full response distributions published for the challenge items.
rob.item6_quote: About 69% of respondents indicated that misleading or false information circulating on social media platforms created confusion regarding the objectives, procedures, and implications of the NIN-SIM registration policy.
rob.item10_quote: Out of the 384 questionnaires administered, 371 were successfully retrieved and found valid for analysis.
